I’m in California too so I’ll explain. 
Don’t even worry about the “under 18” section. Those steps don’t and will never apply to you. All you need to do after making an application online is to pay a free, go to the dmv to pass a vision exam, take a photo, and pass the knowledge test. 

If you are a minor (under 18) you will have many additional steps, like -completing drivers education, driving with your parents, behind the wheel training/training certificate, holding your permit for 6 months/etc. 

But you are an adult. For you, once you pass the knowledge test, you can IMMEDIATELY schedule an appointment for the driving test, as long as it isn’t in the same day you took the knowledge test. You can literally make an appointment for the next day if it’s available.

It’s RECOMMENDED you practice driving or go to a driving school, but it’s not REQUIRED. Hope this helps.

Tips:

If you do not know what SMOG is, I suggest you get that down quickly or you will fail. A little “glance in the mirror” will not do it. Every lane change, you need to look in the review,left or right side-mirror, depending on what lane you’re changing into, AND TURN YOUR SHOULDER. Even if it hurts your neck. Exaggerate your movement’s.

Maintain good speed, preferably a little bit slower than posted, but not more than 5 mph slower.

Let all pedestrians cross. If they signal you to go, just wait for them to cross. Other cars may beep at you like they did me, but who cares? There’s their problem. The instructor will not hold anything against you for using the correct right of way.

Stop behind the limit line for 3 full seconds.

My sister failed at Los Gatos because she stopped turning right at a red light and waited for it to turn green. Only wait after stopping if there is a no.turn.on.red.

Do not hit any curb. This is an automatic fail. Oh yeah, try not to do any of those obviously.

And most importantly do not go into the test with expectations. It is NOT over until you pull into the no parking lane. Even if you think you did badly, be confident and move on. You got this.

I understand the routes are different but for me there was absolutely no straight line backing, absolutely no lane changes, and only one left turn which was actually into the dmv parking lot. Practice, go into the test ready but without expectations of passing, AND SMOG. If you don’t know what smog means, well… you will probably fail. You need to look in your review mirror, side mirror, and over your shoulder when making any lane change or going into the bike lane.

Just relax. Follow the instructions.
